# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.20 (pre-release)

Changes since pre.19. Written and tested by the author's assistant on one Linux machine; **nothing was tried on Windows, macOS or arm64**, and the native file dialogs of the window ("Open/Save project", "Export PDF…") could not be tried at all (the test machine has no dialog provider). A correction first: the pre.19 notes said every command in the guide had been run. That was too much: the installation commands (apt, brew, winget), PDF/UA, CIUS-RO, an HTTPS time-stamp server and veraPDF were not run. The guide lists them as unverified.

**Fixes**
- **Sideways check, second attempt (replaces the pre.19 thresholds).** The pre.19 fix was tuned on one page and was fragile: page 13 of the same tester PDF was still turned by 90°, and the new thresholds missed 2 of 98 genuinely sideways book pages. The check now looks only at letter-sized pieces (0.6–7.6 mm; bigger pieces such as pictures, ornaments and frames do not vote), needs at least 100 of them, and wants the columns at least 3 times stronger than the rows. Measured on 98 book photographs and 5 picture-book pages, each at 0° and rotated 90° (output size compared with pre.18, at 150 and 300 dpi): identical to pre.18 except page 13 (turned wrongly in pre.18, now upright) and one sideways picture page that is no longer turned by this check (Tesseract's OSD and the rotate buttons still work). A corpus of 100 pages is small; please report pages that still turn wrongly.
- **`--redact` now reports and warns.** At the end it prints how many words each pattern covered, warns when a pattern matched nothing, and warns when words that look like an address (domain ending) or a long number are still in the text. The case that exposed it: OCR read `@` as `G`, the e-mail pattern matched nothing, and the address stayed on the page without any message. (The warning is a hint, not a guarantee: a misread value that does not look like an address or number is still not found.) The covered-word count was never printed before.
- Winget manifest points at pre.19.

**Tried in a real window on Linux (not changes, only checks)**: dragging a zone corner, cutting a double sheet at a moved cut line (two pages of 524 and 674 px), saving a profile of your own. Terminal screenshots in the guide are now taken in a real terminal (xterm) instead of drawn.

**Guide**: `LegatorOCR-0.2.0-pre.20-ghid.pdf`, Romanian, updated for these fixes and for the verification above.

**Known limits (unchanged)**: the cut line does not apply to sheets turned by 90° or 270°; OCR can misread characters such as `@`; the rotation behaviour seen on Windows 11 is unconfirmed; Windows, macOS and arm64 builds are untested by the author.
